independent.summary: The in-place reload does not actually preserve zoom/pan/layout, and leaves d3-zoom inconsistent. `initGraph` runs `svg.selectAll('*').remove()` and rebuilds a fresh `<g>` with no transform, while d3-zoom's `defaultTransform` (`this.__zoom || identity`, d3-zoom/src/zoom.js:30,74) keeps the previous gesture state on the same `<svg>` element across the new `svg.call(zoom)`. So after any `group:*` frame the drawing snaps back to identity, yet the zoom behaviour still believes the old transform, and the viewer's next wheel/drag jumps by the stale delta. Node positions are also re-copied from `nodeData` without x/y, so the force layout restarts from scratch. The component docs (GraphView.vue:422-428, 521-528), WikiLayout.vue:1736, docs/architecture.md and the Decision Log all state that the reload keeps "the zoom, the pan and the force layout the viewer is reading" — only the non-remount part of that is true.

The reload test's only evidence for its headline claim is an assertion that cannot fail. `expect(wrapper.find('svg').element).toBe(svgBefore)` is commented "the component was not remounted: the viewer's zoom, pan and layout survive the redraw", but `<svg ref="svgRef">` is static template markup under the same root, so the element identity holds even though `initGraph` wipes every child, re-creates the zoom target with no transform and restarts the simulation from scratch. The test would pass unchanged if zoom, pan and layout were all discarded — which is what the code does.

`entityIds` is flattened downward only, so a write to a nested subgroup leaves the panels that render it stale. `relationshipResolver.resolveGroupLabels` traverses upward and `processGroup` emits `expandedSubGroups`, so an entity that is a member only of parent P has the entity members of child C rendered on its detail panel. A write to C (add/remove/relabel/reorder a member) emits `group:updated` whose `entityIds` is C's subtree, which does not name P's other members, and `groupTouchesPanel` fails its second branch too because that entity's `relationships` holds P, not C. The graph still reloads (it reloads on every frame), but the open detail panel keeps showing the pre-write subgroup membership with no toast — the one thing `entityIds` exists to decide.
